verdict_reason: The helper is correct for the cph gate, but it copies notInUnionOf's union derivation with a different blank rule and renames its lists parameter.

todos.issue: Lines 14-19 copy notInUnionOf's union derivation (not-in-union-of.js lines 27-32: deriveUnion over 'typeof x === function ? x() : x'), so 'resolve the lists, then take their union' now lives in two places. The complement rule also differs between the twins: anyNotInUnionOf skips blank values (line 18, isBlankValue) but notInUnionOf (line 38) counts a blank as outside the union. So one rule, 'value is outside the union', has two homes that disagree.
todos.fix: Must: one function owns resolving and unioning the lists and the 'outside the union' predicate, and both notInUnionOf and anyNotInUnionOf call it, so they treat a blank value the same way. One way: export a resolveUnion(unionOfAllowlists) and an isOutsideUnion(value, union) from internals/derive-union.js and use them in both helpers. If notInUnionOf should keep counting blanks, document that difference in docs/obligation-model.md.

todos.issue: The parameter unionOfLists (line 7) names the same input that its sibling notInUnionOf calls unionOfAllowlists (not-in-union-of.js line 23). That is one concept with two names. Neither name fits: the argument holds the lists (or a getter for them), and the union is derived from it at line 16.
todos.fix: Must: both complement helpers name this parameter with one word that says it holds the lists, not the union. One way: rename it allowlists (or exemptLists) in both any-not-in-union-of.js and not-in-union-of.js.
